transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Severus. The Longbottom family have written to the governors. The letter describes what they call — I quote — 'sustained cruelty' in your classroom. The governors will require a response from me, and I will require one from you. What happened?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Sustained cruelty? Dumbledore, that is a preposterous exaggeration. I merely enforced the rules and maintained a proper standard of discipline in my classroom. The Longbottom boy was disrupting the class, as he often does. I corrected him, nothing more.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I am well aware that Neville Longbottom can be... anxious in your class, Severus. However, the letter speaks of more than a single correction. They describe a pattern of behavior. What, precisely, did you do to correct him?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Dumbledore, I do not make a habit of detailing my disciplinary methods to anyone, least of all to the parents of my students. Suffice it to say that the boy's performance and demeanor in my class have improved. If the Longbottoms are not satisfied with that, it is their problem, not mine.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: It becomes my problem, Severus, when the governors receive such a letter. You are a teacher, not a drill sergeant. "Improved demeanor" achieved through fear is not an improvement I can endorse. I need specifics. What did you say to him? What did you do?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: If you absolutely must know, the boy was allowed to leave the class several times without permission. I informed him that, should he choose to repeat this behavior, he would be confined to the final row for the remainder of the year. This, apparently, was the catalyst for his improved behavior. I fail to see the issue here, Dumbledore.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Confined to the back row for the remainder of the year? For leaving the room? That is not a measured consequence, Severus; it is a punitive sentence. Did you inquire *why* he left the room? Or did you simply assume it was defiance?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Inquire? I do not have the time or the inclination to play nursemaid to every student who claims to be unwell. The boy has a pattern ofidleness andinattentiveness, whichI findto be a greaterconcern than his allegedillnesses. As for your "punitive sentence," it is a perfectly reasonable deterrent to encourage punctuality and attentiveness in my class.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: A deterrent, Severus, or a humiliation? You speak of idleness, but you have not mentioned his work. Has his practical skill improved, or has he merely learned to sit still and be silent? I remind you, we are here to educate, not to intimidate.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Dumbledore, I stand by my methods. The boy's work has improved alongside his behavior. It is my responsibility to ensure that all students in my class learn, not just Neville Longbottom. If his improvement is solely due to fear, then I fail to see how that is any different from the other incentives you employ to motivate your... less... able students.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: The difference, Severus, is that I do not use fear as a tool. I use encouragement, patience, and sometimes, yes, firm guidance. But I do not threaten a child with public isolation for an entire year. You will revise this punishment. Neville will return to his regular seat, effective immediately. And you will, in the future, show a modicum of understanding before you pass judgment. Is that clear?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Dumbledore, I do not respond well to ultimatums. However, I understand that you have your position to maintain. I will rescind the punishment, though I maintain that it was not excessive. As for your suggestion that I 'show understanding,' I hope you are not implying that I should condoneandenableweaknessin my students. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: It is your job to prepare them, Severus, not to break them. The real world holds enough cruelty without us replicating it within these walls. I expect your written response to the governors on my desk by tomorrow evening. It will acknowledge the Longbottoms' concerns and outline the steps you will take to ensure your discipline is fair and proportionate. Do I make myself understood?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Understood, Dumbledore. I will provide the requested response. However, I must note that if this leniency becomes a trend, the quality of education in my classroom will suffer. I do not relish the prospect of having to grade essays on "The Uses of Fluffernutter" and "The Benefits of Endless Detentions," but if the standard of excellence is to be compromised, such measures may become necessary.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your sarcasm is noted, Severus, but it does not serve you here. The standard of excellence is not compromised by basic decency. Provide your response. And remember, I will be paying closer attention to your classroom. That is all.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
